title: Finance & Legal: Integrated Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, and Revenue Recognition Policy
author: Marisol Chen
content:
Purpose

This document defines Redwood Inference’s integrated Finance & Legal policies for annual budgeting and rolling forecasting, contract lifecycle management, procurement approvals and procedures, and revenue recognition & billing practices. The goal is to create a single, auditable source of truth for decisions that materially affect our financial statements, cash flow, commercial risk, and compliance posture.

Scope

Applies to all Redwood Inference business units, subsidiaries, and purchases of goods or services that require a purchase order, contract, or invoice. Includes customer contracts, vendor contracts, procurement of cloud/compute/GPU capacity, software subscriptions, and professional services.

Key Roles and Ownership

- Finance (owner: Finance Controller) – owns budgeting cadence, forecasts, AR, revenue recognition schedules, accounting treatment, and reporting to execs and board.
- Legal (owner: Senior Counsel) – owns contract templates, clause approvals (IP, data, liability), signature authority rules, and legal risk assessment.
- Procurement (owner: Procurement Manager) – owns vendor onboarding, master vendor list, PO issuance, and procurement ops.
- Business Owner (requesting manager) – owns requirements, justification, and budget line ownership.
- Approvers (see Approval Matrix) – provide financial and legal sign-off depending on thresholds.

Section 1 — Budgeting & Forecasting

Overview
- Annual operating budget (AOB) is prepared by Finance with inputs from Product, Engineering, SRE, Sales, and Go-to-market.
- Rolling 12-month forecast is updated monthly and presented to exec leadership on the 5th business day.
- Capital requests (capex) follow the capital approval workflow and are tracked separately from operating budgets.

Cadence and Deliverables
1. Planning kickoff (May): Finance issues templates and targets.
2. Budgets due (July 15): Business units submit line-item budgets with headcount requests.
3. Budget reviews (Aug): Cross-functional reviews and scenario analysis.
4. Final budget & board submission (Sept): CEO + CFO approval.
5. Monthly rolling forecast (updated by 3rd business day each month).
6. Quarterly re-forecast (post-quarter close) for changes >5% of department spend.

Forecasting assumptions must be documented in the submission, including: model assumptions for hosted API growth, expected Dedicated contracts, expected private deployment pipeline, average contract length, and churn assumptions.

KPIs and Controls
- Monthly burn, run-rate, and remaining runway (Finance).
- Annual contract value (ACV) and bookings vs. target (Sales/Finance).
- Variance analysis >10% must be investigated and summarized in the monthly finance pack.

Section 2 — Contracts & Legal Process

Standard Contracts and Templates
- All customer-facing commercial agreements must use Legal-approved templates stored in the contract repository (SharePoint/DocStore). Variants: Standard SaaS MSA, Dedicated Deployment Addendum, Private Deployment SOW, NDA, Professional Services Agreement.
- Vendor contracts must use Legal-approved vendor terms or be reviewed by Legal for exceptions.

Contract Lifecycle Steps (numbered procedure)
1. Initiation: Business Owner opens Contract Request in Legal intake portal (include budget code and expected term).
2. Legal review: Legal triages risk (IP/data, export controls, liability caps) and applies standard template clauses where possible.
3. Commercial negotiation: Sales / Procurement coordinate with Legal on redlines.
4. Approval: Approvals required per Approval Matrix below (finance/legal signatures).
5. Execution: Contracts signed using approved e-signature tool (DocuSign).
6. Post-signature: Legal and Finance record contract metadata (counterparty, start/end dates, ACV, billing cadence, revenue treatment) in the contract registry.
7. Filing & retention: Contracts are retained per records retention policy (minimum 7 years for commercial contracts).

Approval Matrix (table)
| Transaction Type | Threshold | Required Approvals | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Standard vendor subscription | <= $25,000 annual | Requesting manager + Procurement | Use off-the-shelf PO and standard terms |
| Non-standard vendor terms or > $25k | $25,001 – $250,000 | Requesting manager + Procurement + Finance Manager + Legal Counsel | Legal must review data & IP clauses |
| Strategic vendor / > $250k | > $250,000 | Head of Function + Finance Director + VP Legal + Procurement Director | Board notification for multi-year commitments > $2M |
| Customer contracts with non-standard liability/IP | Any | Sales Director + Legal Counsel + Finance Controller | Escalate to GC for high risk |

Signature Authority
- Individual signature matrix is documented in the Delegation of Authority (DoA) appendix. Only authorized signatories (CEO, CFO, VP Sales with delegation) may execute contracts exceeding delegation.

Contract Metadata Table (required fields)
- counterparty_name
- contract_type
- owner (business owner)
- start_date
- end_date
- acv
- billing_cadence (monthly/quarterly/annually/usage)
- revenue_recognition_treatment (subscription/usage/POC)

Section 3 — Procurement Procedures

Procurement Principles
- Prefer approved vendors and enterprise agreements for cloud, GPU, and infrastructure spend.
- Use competitive bidding for purchases > $50k (three bids recommended).
- Obtain Procurement and Finance approval before issuing PO for committed spend.

Procurement Workflow (numbered steps)
1. Requisition: Business Owner submits requisition with justification and budget code in the procurement system (Coupa/OracleNetSuite).
2. Sourcing: Procurement conducts vendor evaluation and validates vendor onboarding checklist (W-9, tax ID, insurance certificates, sanctions screening).
3. Approval: Follow Approval Matrix for sign-off.
4. PO issuance: Procurement issues PO and attaches approved contract/terms.
5. Receipt & invoice: Requesting team confirms receipt of goods/services in the system.
6. Invoice processing: AP matches invoice to PO and processes for payment per payment terms (Net 30 standard).

Vendor Onboarding Checklist (bulleted list)
- Completed vendor profile (legal name, tax ID, remittance address)
- W-9 (US vendors) or equivalent tax form for non-US vendors
- Insurance certificate (as required by contract)
- Data processing addendum if vendor will handle customer data
- Sanctions and AML screening passed

Procurement Escalations & Exceptions
- For exceptions (single-source, sole-source justification), Procurement must prepare an exception memo signed by the Head of Function and CFO.
- Emergency purchases (operational-impacting within 48 hours) can be approved by the Head of Ops and Finance Manager retrospectively documented in the procurement system.

Section 4 — Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies

Revenue Recognition Principles (ASC 606 / IFRS 15 alignment)
- Revenue is recognized when control of promised goods or services is transferred to the customer in an amount that reflects the consideration Redwood expects to receive.
- Contract identification, performance obligations, transaction price determination, allocation, and recognition guidance must be reviewed by Finance Accounting.

Common Scenarios
1. Subscription & Hosted API (recurring, time-based): Recognize ratably over the contract term once the service is available (deferred revenue liability on receipt of prepayment).
2. Dedicated / Reserved Capacity (multi-month commitments): Recognize over the committed period unless significant performance obligations remain; discounts/credits documented and allocated.
3. Usage-based billing (metered tokens/embeddings): Recognize when usage occurs or when billable measurement is determinable each month; estimate variable consideration conservatively if material.
4. Professional services (implementation): Separate PS into distinct performance obligations when the service provides benefit on its own; otherwise recognize over time based on percentage of completion.

Billing & Invoicing Standards
- Standard billing cadence: Monthly in arrears for usage-based; monthly/quarterly/annual in advance for subscription per contract.
- Invoices must include: invoice number, contract reference, billing period, line-item detail (quantity, unit price, discounts), tax details, remittance instructions.
- All invoices routed through AP and tracked in accounting system (NetSuite). Disputed invoices entered as dispute tickets with resolution SLA of 14 calendar days.

Credit & Collections
- Standard payment terms: Net 30 for customers (exceptions require Finance approval).
- Late payment interest: 1.5% per month after 30 days on unpaid balances unless prohibited by contract.
- Collections escalation: 30 days past due – Customer Success outreach; 60 days – Finance collections; 90 days – escalate to Legal for contractual remedies.

Revenue Cutover & Close Controls
- Monthly close checklist includes deferred revenue ledger review, contract milestone testing, and recognition sign-off by Finance Controller.
- Sample close checklist items: reconcile new contracts recorded, verify billing terms mapped to recognition policy, confirm no unrecorded liabilities.

Section 5 — Auditability, Records, and Retention

- Contract repository must store executed copies and metadata (see Contract Metadata Table).
- Procurement records (POs, SOWs, invoices) retained for minimum 7 years.
- Revenue contracts and key billing records retained for 7 years; longer retention for disputes or regulatory reasons.
- Periodic internal audits (Finance Ops) scheduled annually; external auditors will be provided access under NDA.

Appendices
A. Quick Checklist for Sales (pre-signature)
- Confirm template selection, liability caps, and data processing addendum.
- Validate ACV, billing cadence, and revenue treatment with Finance.
- Submit contract request in Legal intake portal with required metadata.

B. Purchase & Contract Approval Quick Reference (summary)
- <= $25k standard vendor: manager + procurement
- $25k–$250k: add Finance Manager + Legal Counsel
- > $250k: add Head of Function + Finance Director + VP Legal
- Multi-year commitments > $2M: Board notification

C. Example Invoice Line Item (text sample)
- Redwood Inference — Hosted API Usage
- Billing period: 2027-01-01 to 2027-01-31
- Token usage: 12,345,678 tokens at $0.0004/token = $4,938.27
- Discounts/Credits: $0.00
- Total Due: $4,938.27

Contact & Escalation

- Procurement Manager: procurement@redwood.ai
- Legal intake: legal-intake@redwood.ai
- Escalation: finance-escalations@redwood.ai (use for AR > 60 days or disputed > $50k)
